items.title: 8.16.1 Synthesis of ammonia by Haber's process

source_refs.note: Topic 8.16.1, printed pages 183-184 (Table 8.1 and Figure 8.4), with the second Quick Check 8.6 as the self-check. The print cites 'Table 8.2' and 'Figure 8.3' for Table 8.1 and Figure 8.4.

blocks.text: Ammonia synthesis from nitrogen and hydrogen is reversible: N2(g) + 3H2(g) giving 2NH3(g), delta H = -46.11 kJ per mol. The maximum yield is obtained in three ways: decrease the concentration of ammonia by removing it from the vessel from time to time, so that the equilibrium shifts forward by Le Chatelier's principle; use high pressure, since four moles of reactants give two moles of product and the reaction proceeds with decreasing volume, so high pressure shifts the equilibrium to the right; and lower the temperature, since the reaction is exothermic and cooling shifts it forward. Table 8.1 and the yield graph show that the effect of pressure and temperature on the yield is very prominent: the most complete conversion is 98.3 per cent at 473 K (200 degrees C) and 1000 atm. At 200 degrees C the yield is favoured but the rate becomes very slow and the process uneconomic, so the temperature is raised to a moderate 400 degrees C and a catalyst is used to increase the rate; the same rate without a catalyst would need a much higher temperature, which lowers the yield.

blocks.caption: Effect of temperature on Kc for ammonia synthesis (Table 8.1)

items: Catalyst: pieces of iron crystals in a fused mixture of MgO, Al2O3 and SiO2.

blocks.prompt: How does the proportion of ammonia in the N2, H2, NH3 system change as the temperature rises, what is the sign of delta H, and what happens to Kp when the temperature is raised?
blocks.explanation: The proportion of ammonia falls as the temperature rises, as the falling Kc values of Table 8.1 and the yield curves show. Delta H is negative, -46.11 kJ per mol as printed, the reaction being exothermic. By Le Chatelier's principle raising the temperature favours the reverse, endothermic direction, so Kp, like Kc, decreases.

items: N2 + 3H2 giving 2NH3, exothermic, 4 gas moles to 2: yield rises with pressure, with removal of ammonia and with lower temperature (98.3 per cent at 200 degrees C and 1000 atm), but low temperature is too slow.
Optimum: 200 to 300 atm, about 673 K, iron catalyst in fused MgO, Al2O3 and SiO2; Kc falls from 7.15 x 10^15 at 200 K to 3.96 x 10^-2 at 800 K.
